title: Wolf Creek
tagline: Stay off the dirt roads. Stay for dinner.
about: Three backpackers on an outback road trip run into a friendly bushman who turns out to be anything but.

Rub the butter into the flour until crumbly.Mix in the milk with a knife until it just comes together.Shape into a round, score the top and bake. Or wrap around green sticks over coals.Serve with butter and golden syrup.Road trip honey soy roasted nutsThe long drive across WAHow to make itAs written, serves 4Cashews, almonds and peanuts roasted in honey, soy, chilli and sesame until glossy and crunchy, tossed with dried mango and bagged up for the car.Heat the oven to 160°C.Warm 3 tbsp honey with 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil and half a teaspoon of chilli flakes.Toss through 200g cashews, 150g almonds and 150g peanuts with 1 tbsp sesame seeds.Spread on a lined tray and roast 20 to 25 minutes, stirring twice, until golden.Cool fully on the tray, break up and mix with 100g chopped dried mango.Smoked kangaroo jerkyCut by Mick. breadHow to make it8 thick beef sausages2 onions, sliced30g butter8 slices of white breadtomato sauce, to serveCook the sausages slowly over low coals or a barbecue, turning often.Fry the onions in the butter on the hotplate until soft and golden.Fold each sausage into bread with onions and sauce.Broome beer-battered barramundi and chipsThe coast at Broome where the trip beginsHow to make itAs written, serves 4Barramundi fillets in a crisp lager batter, fried golden, with thick chips, lemon wedges and a homemade tartare sauce of capers, gherkin and dill.Cut 1kg potatoes into thick chips and fry at 140°C for 6 minutes, drain, then again at 180°C for 3 minutes.Whisk 200g plain flour, 1 tsp baking powder and salt with 300ml cold lager.Dust 800g barramundi pieces in flour, dip in batter and fry at 180°C for 4 to 5 minutes.Mix 150g mayonnaise with chopped capers, gherkins, dill and lemon for tartare.SweetsGolden syrup dumplingsSoft dumplings simmered in a golden syrup and brown sugar
